decision.explanation: Since y₂ = −x₂ and y₁ = x₁ + 2x₂, we have x₂ = −y₂ and x₁ = y₁ + 2y₂. Substituting gives Q = (y₁ + 2y₂)² − 3(y₁ + 2y₂)y₂ + y₂² = y₁² + y₁y₂ − y₂².

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & =-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for ${x}_{2}$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =-{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =({y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})^{2}+3({y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})(-{y}_{2})+(-{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}-3{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-6{y}_{2}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Given that [y1y2]=[120−1][x1x2], express the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+3x1x2+x22 in terms of the components of y.

a
y12−2y1y2+y22
b
y12−y22
c
y12+y1y2−y22
d
y12+5y1y2−2y22
e
y12−3y1y2+y22
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that

[y1y2]=[120−1][x1x2]

gives the following expressions for y1 and y2:

y1=x1+2x2y2=−x2

By solving the second equation for x2 and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for x1 and x2:

x1=y1+2y2x2=−y2

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

Q(x)=x12+3x1x2+x22=(y1+2y2)2+3(y1+2y2)(−y2)+(−y2)2=y12+4y1y2+4y22−3y1y2−6y22+y22=y12+y1y2−y22

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms x₁ = y₁ + 2y₂ and x₂ = −y₂. Substitution yields Q = y₁² + (4−3)y₁y₂ + (4−6+1)y₂² = y₁² + y₁y₂ − y₂², matching option c. The displayed incorrect submission selected b, which omits the cross term.

content.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & =-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for ${x}_{2}$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =-{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =({y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})^{2}+3({y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})(-{y}_{2})+(-{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}-3{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-6{y}_{2}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The transformation gives y₁ = x₂ and y₂ = −x₁, so x₁ = −y₂ and x₂ = y₁. Substituting yields Q = (−y₂)² + (−y₂)y₁ − 2y₁² = −2y₁² − y₁y₂ + y₂².

after.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & =-{x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving these for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & ={y}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(-{y}_{2})^{2}+(-{y}_{2}){y}_{1}-2{y}_{1}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}-{y}_{2}{y}_{1}-2{y}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-2{y}_{1}^{2}-{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that [y1y2]=[01−10][x1x2], express the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+x1x2−2x22 in terms of the components of y.

a

y12−2y1y2+y22

−2y12−y1y2+y22

EXPLANATION

First, notice that

[y1y2]=[01−10][x1x2]

gives the following expressions for y1 and y2:

y1=x2y2=−x1

Solving these for x1 and x2, we obtain the following:

x1=−y2x2=y1

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

Q(x)=x12+x1x2−2x22=(−y2)2+(−y2)y1−2y12=y22−y2y1−2y12=−2y12−y1y2+y22

content.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & =-{x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving these for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & ={y}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(-{y}_{2})^{2}+(-{y}_{2}){y}_{1}-2{y}_{1}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}-{y}_{2}{y}_{1}-2{y}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-2{y}_{1}^{2}-{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ 10 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}21 & 26 \\ 26 & 32\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]

after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 13 \\ 3 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}47 & 30 \\ 30 & 19\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}\,-1 & -1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}\,-1 & -1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\,-1 & -1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\,-1 & -1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\,-1 & -1 \\ 1 & \,\,-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
